findings.reason: a node building §9 as written either leaves its own cited plan-carrying review without a rubric or silently stops the plan gates running for plan-carrying review runs, and the done-when would not catch either.
findings.text: §9 routes every run review's rubric through a composed brief, but `brief = "" if plan else node.brief_path` and `_review_dispatch_tokens` choose `--brief` XOR `--plan/--section`, so making the brief non-empty for a plan-naming run replaces `--plan/--section` with `--brief` and drops the plan authority the in-code invariant at recovery_review_subject.py:496-502 says such a run must keep; §9 states no such change and its done-when tests only an implement run and an investigate run, so the plan-carrying example it cites is neither shown fixed nor shown safe

findings.reason: §8 has already landed, so the dependency is satisfied and no schedule or gate changes; recording it is bookkeeping rather than a change to what a node does.
findings.text: §9's deliverable composes `load_claims_review_prompt` for a read-only run, a loader §8 adds, yet the s9 section element carries `data-links=""` and no ordering prose, so the s9-to-s8 dependency is not declared

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `load_review_prompt`/`load_claims_review_prompt` (review.py:432/437), `_review_dispatch_fields` (recovery_review_subject.py:355) and `_review_dispatch_action` (recovery_classification.py:550, a live call site) all resolve, and the plan no longer cites the blank line 411.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §9 names a measurable test and a declared, executed negative control (compose the brief from the reviewed run's brief alone; the first assertion fails).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the cited prompt file resolves on the durable crew-runs path (141 lines, present) and the test path is a repository test file.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §9 introduces no plan labels, ticket numbers or version tags; `SCORE <dimension>` and `CLAIM` are emitted-record grammar, not symbols.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §9's mechanism cannot reach the plan-carrying run its own cited example is about without a change §9 does not state: `_review_dispatch_fields` sets `brief=""` whenever the reviewed run names a plan, so a plan-carrying review dispatches `--plan/--section` and never a brief, and plan-carrying is exactly the case of the cited `r-20261010T204459845050-review-of-a-read-takes-no-lock/prompt.txt` (its prompt carries `PLAN reckon:a-read-answers-inside-its-deadline §2`).
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §9 carries one deliverable, composing the run review's brief from the rubric.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §9 composes `load_claims_review_prompt`, which §8 introduces, but the §9 section element declares no relationship (`data-links=""`), so the dependency it rests on is unrecorded.
